chapter: Stockton, Pacific and the Army years
title: Pearlman, Studs Terkel's The Good War and the Cronkite recording
summary: The man who built the truck changed his name to Waxman and appears in Terkel's book; Brubeck also recorded Private Brubeck Remembers with Walter Cronkite.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Leroy Pearlman has mentioned that the Wolf Pack once played on a show with Marlene Dietrich.
That’s the guy that built the truck, Pearlman.
He also said the band worked on the same bill as other well-known performers. Do you have any . . .?
Pearlman changed his name to Waxman. If you want to check up on him, Studs Terkel’s book The Good War has an interview with him, and Waxman starts talking about me.
Yeah, I’ve seen the book. Yes. It’s about the Battle of the Bulge.
And the Bulge has a good story with – that’s how it was – who did we do that recording with, Dave Remembers? Walter Cronkite.

Private Brubeck Remembers. Cronkite is talking about the Bulge, his memory of it, with me. You can get that from George Moore at my house, because they only allowed 10,000 copies with that CD to be released. They’re all gone, but George has made a tape of it.
